title: Palace: BARMM parliamentary polls generally peaceful
summary: MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang on Tuesday said the first Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) parliamentary elections were generally peaceful and orderly despite several violent…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang on Tuesday said the first Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) parliamentary elections were generally peaceful and orderly despite several violent incidents that left four people dead.
After four postponements, the region’s first parliamentary elections finally pushed through on Monday, Sept. 14.
Violent incidents, including clashes in Cotabato City left four people dead and at least 20 others injured, which marred the historic elections.

“Although hindi nanaisin ng Pangulo at ng administrasyon na ito na mayroon pong nangyayaring karahasan at ito naman po ang ipinag-uutos ng Pangulo na bantayan mabuti, protektahan ang ating mga kababayan sa mga ganitong klaseng insidente but nag-report na po ang PNP, according to PNP, generally peaceful and orderly po iyong naganap na eleksyon. So, sa pananaw po ng administrasyon ay naging maganda naman po ang naging eleksyon kahapon sa BARMM,” Palace press officer Claire Castro said.

(Although the President and this administration hoped that violence will not erupt, and this is what he ordered, to protect the people from violence, the PNP reported that the elections were generally peaceful. Hence the administration thinks that yesterday’s BARMM elections went smoothly.)
Castro said President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. opposed any form of violence and had ordered authorities to closely monitor such incidents and protect voters.

“Kahit isang tao lang po ang nasaktan hindi po ikasasaya ng Pangulo, kahit sabihin po natin generally peaceful and orderly iyong nangyaring eleksiyon kahapon basta po mayroong kahit isa na nasaktan hindi po magiging maganda ang pakiramdam ninuman lalung-lalo na ng Pangulo,” she also said.

(Even if only one person was injured, that would not make the President happy. Even if we say that yesterday’s election was generally peaceful and orderly, as long as even one person was hurt, no one would feel good about it, especially the President.)

“Initial reports show a high voter turnout of 82.41 percent, which may still increase as the remaining voting centers complete the voting process. This is 4.79 percentage points higher than the 77.62 percent voter turnout recorded in BARMM during the May 2025 national and local elections,” said Castro
“According to PNP, all election paraphernalia have already been accounted for and returned. So far, no other significant untoward incidents had been reported,” she continued.
The PNP is also coordinating with the Comelec and other concerned agencies as the remaining election activities are completed.
For its part, the Comelec highlighted the more than 82 percent voter turnout despite reported incidents of violence and compromised ballots.
According to the election body’s central server, the latest data showed voter turnout at 82.9 percent, equivalent to 1,984,331 of the region’s 2,393,202 registered voters.
The parliamentary elections have yet to conclude, as voting resumed in parts of Maluso, Basilan, after it was postponed on Monday.
Voting was suspended after the Comelec discovered that ballots in 36 of the town’s 68 precincts had already been pre-shaded, compromising the integrity of the voting process. /gsg
